{{Short description|Theorem about the distribution of primes}}
The '''Erdős–Delange theorem''' is a theorem in [[number theory]] concerning the distribution of [[prime number]]s. It is named after [[Paul Erdős]] and Hubert Delange.

Let <math>\omega(n)</math> denote the number of prime factors of an integer <math>n</math>, counted with multiplicity, and <math>\lambda</math> be any [[irrational number]].  The theorem states that the real numbers <math>\lambda\omega(n)</math> are asymptotically uniformly distributed modulo 1.{{r|delange}} It implies the [[prime number theorem]].{{r|bergelson-richter}}

The theorem was stated without proof in 1946 by [[Paul Erdős]], with a remark that "the proof is not easy".{{r|erdos}} Hubert Delange found a simpler proof and published it in 1958, together with two other ways of deducing it from results of Erdős and of [[Atle Selberg]].{{r|delange}}
